As per order no.304-A dated 21.08.2025, 26.08.2025 this Court directed the concerned Authority to file affidavit on the issue as to whether the Puja Committees are taking prior permission relating to the nature of pandals (both bamboo and electrical), the height of gates and its numbers to be constructed within their respective areas while applying for licenses and what safety measures are being taken by the Puja Committee for maintenance of such pandals and whether no objection certificates are issued by taking into account all the safety measures.
Needless to say, roads are public spaces meant for the use of all citizens.
Blocking them infringes on the public right to free movement.
The dangers of a Puja Mandap gate across the road are Registrar (Judicial) vs State Of Odisha & Others .... Opp. ...

3 significant, creating risks for both public safety and traffic flow.
Mandap gates built on public roads cause severe traffic congestion and block access for emergency vehicles like ambulances, trucks and fire brigade vehicles.
Being temporary structures, these gates are vulnerable to heavy rain and wind.
A collapse can damage vehicles and cause serious injuries even death.
Many gates feature intricate electrical decorations, faulty wiring which when exposed to weather poses fire hazard and a risk of electrocution to passerby.
The structures can create bottlenecks that make it difficult to manage large crowds.
This is especially risky during emergencies when people need to be evacuated quickly.

Right from the starting of construction of pandals across the public road which used to start two to three weeks prior to Puja till its complete removal, it creates public inconvenience, traffic problem and risk to the lives of public at any moment.

Last year, apart from Khan Nagar Durga Puja welcome gate collapsed near the CNBT in Cuttack, on 06.10.2024 afternoon, Bhubaneswar faced a heavy downpour leading to the collapse of a 30-feet high pandal gate at the Rasulgarh Durga Puja Committee.
The 20-foot wide light gate, unable to withstand the gusty winds accompanying the rain, caused significant traffic snarls in the area.
Similar collapses of Puja Pandal gate at Damana in Bhubaneswar sparked fear among the people to come out of the houses.
The devotees gathered at the Puja Pandal had a close shave when the Pandal collapsed as reported in the media on 04.10.2022.
Puja Pandal collapse incidents were also reported in the media from Vyasanagar in Jajpur district and Raghunathpur Bazar in the district of Jagatsinghpur.
The competitiveness among Durga Puja Committees is seen through efforts to attract more visitors and sponsors by hosting unique and innovative theme-based Pandals.

This competitive spirit is also fuelled by large-scale events with significant media attention, which leads to more public and financial support and elevates the prestige of the organizing Committee, but all the same, on the altar of competitiveness, public safety, public inconvenience and public lives cannot be sacrificed.

The past experiences have led the District Administration to take corrective measures in this regard with the active cooperation of the Puja Committees as per the suggestion of this Court, which is really heartening.

sentences.text:
(iii) It is relevant to mention here that as per clause 11 of P1 Agreement executed with all contractors, "The amount of security money to be deposited by the tenderer whose tender is selected for acceptance shall be (7 or 5 percent) of the estimated value of the work and towards this amount,
the earnest money already deposited by him shall be credited."
Accordingly in all agreements security deposit of (7 or 5 percent) is being withheld from the agencies until the defect liability period is over.

Further, as per Clause 78 of D.T.C.N. of P1 Agreement, "any defects, shrinkage or other faults which may be noticed within defect liability period, i.e., 12 to 36 months from the completion of the work arising out of defective or improper materials or workmanship, upon the direction of the Engineer-in-Charge are to be amended and made good by the contractor at his own cost unless the Engineer for reasons to be recorded in writing shall decide that they ought to be paid for and in case of default, Department may recover from the contractor the cost of making good the works.
The defect liability period for the work is 12 to 36 months from the date of successful completion of the work".

As per the clauses mentioned above, there is provision for withholding of the amount of the contractors as performance security/ security deposit until completion of defect liability period for one to three years and making the contractors liable to pay compensation to the Government in case there is defect arises during or after construction of road work.
The said affidavit is taken on record.
The Superintendent, R & B shall explore the possibility of extending the deficit liability period to 36 months for all contractors instead of 12 months.
